R7476.summary: Probably Chomentowski to Hetman Sieniawski from Constantinople, dated May-August 1714 because code XVIII is glossed Hospodar Multański (Brâncoveanu, held in Yedikule from April 1714). New passages include "on z tąd nie ruszy, póki mu Porta nie da takiego konwoju", "z listu przejętego", "sołtan gałga uciekł do Czerkies" and "donieść Jmci Panu Kanclerzowi Koronnemu".

R7484-R7485.summary: Chomentowski, voivode of Mazovia and Polish envoy at the Porte, to Hetman Sieniawski: the Kapudan Pasha, made vizier, began to change course; a public divan on 24 April declared war sub ignoto nomine, with fear of a march on Chocim and the envoys sent to Yedikule; on the 26th the vizier was deposed and strangled, so things are in confusion.
R7484-R7485.en:
p. 111
Monseigneur.
I wrote to Your Grace in my last letter by way of Vienna that new changes keep being made here.
Today [?they agree] [...] spoils the resolution.
The Kapudan Pasha, having become vizier, began to change; some say that he has now been talked round, others that
he is still in Istanbul.
For having confidence [...] of the ferman, and to me this [...] could be.
He [?went] as if to visit the King of Sweden, but since he did not want to be at his quarters, only in a third place,
he came back without

p. 112
seeing the King.
On the next day after, the 24th of April, he held a public divan, at which war was declared sub ignoto nomine [under
no named enemy]; whence non vanus [is] our metus [our fear is not groundless].
And so it was to turn towards Chocim, and us to the Yedikule;

snip.cap: R7485: the syllabary, glossed syllable by syllable
snip.credit: Archiwum Narodowe w Krakowie, Zbiór Dzieduszyckich 24/11 no. 116, p. 115, via DECODE R7485

system: A three-digit syllabary in alphabetical bands (a 6-8, b 14-21 ... z 320-333), each band headed by names (Cesarz 42, Moskwa 160, Turcy 271), with Roman-numeral codes (XVIII = Hospodar Multanski); dot-separated, clear words between; Polish.
